title: Perfect quotient coefficients give invertible tower and finite projections
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subset A$ an ideal such that every $A/I^{n+1}$ is perfect over $A$, and $f:Y\to X$ a morphism of small sites. Then, with the strict-tower projection and the finite projection of [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison], for every $H\in D(X,A)$ the tower projection $(Ru_*H)\otimes^L(\underline{A/I^{n+1}})_n\to Ru^J_*(H\otimes^L(\underline{A/I^{n+1}})_n)$ and, for every $n$, the finite projection $Ru_*H\otimes^L_A\underline{A/I^{n+1}}\to Ru_{*}(H\otimes^L_A\underline{A/I^{n+1}})$ over $A/I^{n+1}$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tags 07A4, 0B56, 0941 and 099M; split from completed projection coherence proof

proof.text: Represent $A/I^{n+1}$ by a bounded complex of finite projective $A$-modules. The constant-module functor is exact, so this represents the constant coefficient sheaf and keeps every finite-free retraction. Compute the direct image on a K-injective representative. The finite-projective totalization projection formula [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization] gives an inverse to the counit-tensor projection with this coefficient complex; its representative formula identifies it with the underlying restriction of the finite projection, through the normalized scalar/pullback comparison and finite adjunction of [lem-sp-completion-mate-comparison]. Restriction of quotient coefficients is exact and conservative, so the finite projection is invertible. Evaluating the strict-tower projection at each index gives the same finite projection through the specified evaluation and scalar-restriction comparisons; its cone is acyclic at every index, and cohomology of strict towers is computed levelwise [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian], so the tower projection is invertible. The zero quotient is included.

theorem perfectQuotientProjection (f : Morphism Y X) (h : PerfectQuotients A I) :
    (∀ H : X.derived A, IsIso (f.towerProjection A I H)) ∧
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (H : X.derived A), IsIso (f.finiteProjection A I n H)
